recovery_balance.meaning: HRV z-score minus load z-score; below 0 = load outpacing recovery

aerobic_decoupling_pct.note: first-half vs second-half efficiency drift; under 5% = aerobically sound

drivers: HRV is elevated (+18.6% vs baseline), but sleep is chronically insufficient (5.0h avg, 14/14 nights <7h), resting HR has dropped (-7.3% vs baseline) — a sign of parasympathetic dominance masking fatigue rather than true recovery
Training readiness score is critically low (latest = 17, 7-day avg = 34.5)
Recovery balance is neutral (1.27), but ACWR = 1.3 sits at upper edge of optimal — and load has spiked to 625 TRIMP in one week (June), while recent recovery signals are weak
Body battery is modestly improved (+7.7%), but stress is down (-13.0%) likely due to reduced activity, not resilience
readiness.guidance: This athlete is not recovered enough for quality training; the priority this week is sleep restoration and neural recovery — not volume or intensity.

monthly_review.summary: July shows meaningful aerobic progress (VO2max +2.7%, efficiency improved slightly) but with concerning physiological trade-offs: cadence increased sharply while pace slowed, aerobic TE rose, and decoupling worsened — suggesting fatigue is compromising economy.
monthly_review.highlight: Cadence dropped 33 spm from June to July — the largest single-month change in the 4-month history — coinciding with rising aerobic TE and worsening decoupling, indicating neuromuscular fatigue is overriding aerobic gains.

goal_tracker.message: Chasing 82.4 km in the remaining 31 days is not advisable — current readiness (training readiness score 17), chronic sleep debt (14/14 nights <7h), and compromised decoupling (7.09%) indicate the body is not prepared to absorb that load safely. Prioritizing recovery now will yield better long-term volume adherence and performance than forcing it.

insights.title: Chronic sleep debt correlates with deteriorating running economy
insights.body: Sleep averaged only 5.0h (vs 4.4h baseline), yet running economy worsened from 13.42 (May) to 13.64 (July); recent RE values show volatility (234.6 → 262.2 → 257.0), consistent with poor sleep impairing metabolic consistency and neuromuscular coordination.

insights.title: Load spike in late June preceded sharp rise in aerobic decoupling
insights.body: The highest weekly TRIMP (625) occurred in June — followed by July’s median decoupling (7.11%) doubling May’s (2.7%) and exceeding the 5% aerobic threshold; this suggests accumulated fatigue is now manifesting as mid-run efficiency collapse.

insights.title: Elevated HRV masks suppressed autonomic resilience
insights.body: HRV is up (+11.2 ms), but resting HR dropped (-3.8 bpm) and training readiness is critically low (17) — classic signs of 'parasympathetic overreach', where the nervous system is fatigued but compensating via vagal dominance, not true recovery.

insights.title: Cadence collapse reflects neuromuscular fatigue, not fitness loss
insights.body: Cadence fell from 151 spm (June) to 118 spm (July) despite faster average pace (518 vs 539 sec/km), and ground contact time increased (309–319 ms across recent runs) — evidence of reduced stride elasticity and propulsion efficiency under fatigue.

recommendations.action: Complete 3 consecutive nights of ≥7.5 hours of sleep — no screens after 21:00, room temperature ≤20°C, no caffeine after 13:00
recommendations.reason: 14/14 nights <7h sleep is the dominant recovery deficit and directly impairs HRV stabilization, decoupling control, and running economy

recommendations.action: Perform 10 minutes of guided diaphragmatic breathing (5s inhale / 5s exhale) daily before bed, tracked via HRV app
recommendations.reason: To support vagal tone re-calibration and shift from parasympathetic overreach toward balanced autonomic function

recommendations.action: Replace all running with walking (4.5–5.5 km, HR <115 bpm) on Monday, Wednesday, and Friday — zero zones, zero pace targets
recommendations.reason: Current readiness score (17) and decoupling (7.09%) contraindicate running; walking preserves circulation and neuromuscular priming without adding load

risk_flags.evidence: Training readiness 17, resting HR 49 bpm (↓3.8 vs baseline), HRV 69.0 ms (↑ but contextually misleading), sleep <7h ×14 days
risk_flags.action: Pause all structured training for 5 days; prioritize sleep, hydration, and vagal stimulation

risk_flags.evidence: Aerobic decoupling 7.09% (↑ from 2.7% in May), VO2max stable (39.0) but running economy worsening (13.64), vertical oscillillation unchanged (~7.7–7.9 cm) despite longer ground contact (309–370 ms)
risk_flags.action: Eliminate all Zone 3+ efforts for 10 days; reassess decoupling after 3 fully recovered runs

risk_flags.evidence: Cadence dropped 33 spm, ground contact increased up to 370 ms (July 31), stride length decreased (74.46–79.92 cm vs 83.4–86.42 cm in fresher runs), vertical oscillillation remained high (~7.7 cm) — inefficient force application pattern
risk_flags.action: Zero hill work, zero speed drills, zero barefoot or minimalist footwear for next 2 weeks

weekly_focus.description: This week prioritizes restoring autonomic balance and circadian rhythm before reintroducing running stimulus — using sleep duration, breathwork, and low-impact movement to rebuild foundational resilience.

Mobility flow (15 min: hip CARs, calf rockers, supine knee-to-chest with diaphragmatic breath)
